text:
ashwin: Heads-up — RFC follow-up: proposal to break the large 'runtime-control' surface into 3 logical facets (routing, session-ownership, and health/metrics). Want to align on sequencing and ownership before I draft the cutover playbook. pinging folks who worked on session mesh and the orchestration split.
maria: Love the idea. Can you sketch the invariants each facet needs to preserve? e.g., session affinity, KV cache ownership, and fallback routing.
ashwin: typo — meant @ashwin :sweat_smile:
ashwin: Good catch, maria. Quick sketch:
```
- routing: deterministic placement + fallback policy
- session-ownership: KV cache lifecycle and lease semantics
- health/metrics: liveness/probing + latency SLO emitters
```
kevin: High-level Q — why 3 facets and not separating by hotpath vs control? feels like we've mixed runtime concerns with control-plane ones before and it bit us.
maria: Because hotpath (token path) needs tight coupling with session-ownership for KV and cache locality. Routing decisions need to be low-latency and two hops away from hotpath if possible. health/metrics can be separately operated but needs strong contract for SLO-based traffic shaping.
lucy: Suggestion: define a stable RPC boundary for each facet now (protobuf contract) and implement adapters that can be toggled by feature flag. That will let teams iterate on impl without changing the contract.
nashwin: agreed — sample proto sketch:
```
service Routing {
  rpc Route(Request) returns (RouteDecision) {}
}
message RouteDecision {
  string target_pool = 1;
  bool fall_back = 2;
}
```
maria: +1. Also add an event stream from session-ownership -> health for cache-miss spikes; ops can react before user impact.
kevin: Risk callout: cross-facet transactions (e.g., allocate session then route) could cause partial failures. We need explicit idempotency and compensating ops. Maybe maintain an allocation lease with TTL and finalizer API.
lucy: For cutover, propose 3-phase plan: 1) stabilize contracts + adapters behind flags, 2) run duplicate traffic to new facets (shadowing) for 48-72h, 3) gradual traffic flip with canaries and automatic rollback based on health metrics.
nashwin: sounds good. We should also list ownership per slice: routing -> infra-networking, session-ownership -> eng-runtime, health/metrics -> observability. Any objections?
maria: No objections. One ask: can eng-runtime take a small team rotation to own the session-ownership rollouts for first 6 weeks? they know the cache code best.
kevin: ops note: make sure the rollout emits detailed traces so we can debug cross-facet latency. Add a short-term SLI for 'cross-facet latency p95 < 30ms' during canary.
lucy: I'll draft the proto + adapter skeleton and open a spike PR. Will include a test harness that replays production traces (anonymized) for shadowing.
ashwin: Awesome. Action items: lucy - proto+PR by EOD Thursday; maria - write event API contract for cache-miss spikes; kevin - draft rollback guardrails and SLI definitions; ashwin - draft cutover playbook and timeline.
infra-bot: CI pipeline triggered for branch "facet-extract/proto-skeleton" — build queued. :robot_face: 
maria: tiny nit — add a migration section for client libraries that call the old runtime-control API. We need a shim for 1 quarter so clients can migrate.
kevin: Also callout cost estimate: more RPC hops may increase infra egress. I'll run a cost delta against current traffic patterns in the spike.
lucy: Noted. I'll include a perf run with the shadowed traces.
ashwin: Thanks team. If no objections I'll convert this into the follow-up RFC and tag in the owners. :rocket:
